Hatred es sin duda alguna, un milagro técnico.
Hace ya mucho tiempo vengo queriendo escribir una reseña sobre este juego, viendo la falta de opiniones desarrolladas bajo el léxico hispano. I don't know what to say tho…
Hatred es un juego violento, crudo, y por mucho que me pese decirlo, un poco edgy. Es un juego fuertemente inspirado en lo que fue el primer Postal, y no tiene nada que envidiarle (excepto por el rendimiento, duhh)
Como todo es de un modo u otro biased, no me voy a molestar en ocultarlo, ahora si mucha intro!!
Hatred te mantiene atrapado en un mundo a blanco y negro que logra asemejarse mucho a la realidad, un mundo en el que cada muerte se siente como si de verdad le estuvieras poniendo fin a una vida, pero sin la carga moral que esto conlleva. Tiene muchísimas animaciones y momentos del gameplay que parecieran diseñados específicamente para ser retratados eternamente, dándote la opción como jugador de enmarcarlos ya sea como un video o foto. 
Yendo por el apartado vanilla del juego, es bastante bueno, aunque no lo considero mejor que el Postal Redux ni en pedo. Tiene una vista isométrica y podes marcar los objetos, civiles y policías en un tono rojo brillante con tan solo tocar un botón, en caso de que te este costando. De todos modos, donde este juego brilla, es en el apartado de su comunidad; Una comunidad que es activa incluso a día de hoy, la cual comparte sus experiencias, cultura, y lo mejor, una gamma de mods que mejoran el juego de forma absurda. El mas destacado siendo un mod que te permite jugar en primera persona y otras perspectivas de cámara. Mods como estos incluyen muchas cosas, como modificaciones a la apariencia del juego, cheats, y básicamente, una personalización total (o casi) de cada uno de los aspectos del juego. Personalmente, yo lo disfruto mas en primera persona, con algo de musica y el sonido configurado para que se sienta como si tuviera auriculares en medio de la situación; No hay nada mejor que el sonido de los disparos eclipsando la musica lo justo y necesario.
Hay algunos diálogos que son geniales, y tienen tanta emoción que perfectamente podrían pasar como reales. Como todo buen voice acting, no?! Nada nuevo jeje.    
La banda sonora también es muy buena, va, es genial. No puedo decir mucho por que como dije antes, no la escucho a la hora de jugar, ni nunca, jejeje. Pero es genial! Lo ultimo que quiero es que piensen que este juego decae por ahí.
Por ultimo, pero no menos importante, en realidad, es muy importante....
Vieron que al principio dije que es un milagro técnico? Bueno, es un juego que tiende a andar como el traste. Si no tenes una compu buena, ya te digo yo que te va a ir muy mal aunque este sea un juego del 2015. La parte difícil de pasarte este juego es que va a haber bajones de fps como si fueran mosquitos en verano, al punto de que en los últimos niveles puede llegar a hacerse injugable. Esto pasa por sobre todo con mods. En vanilla es mas "relajado", por así decirlo. Pero incluso con todo eso, es un juego que vale la pena completamente, en especial teniendo en cuenta que te sale menos de un dólar cuando esta en descuento. 
No sé como terminar esto, fin de la reseña, supongo? Ba-bye

Postal 1, with none of the gameplay, atmosphere, or narrative, Hatred is possibly the worst isometric shooter I've ever played.

1. The movement is stiff and unresponsive, getting caught on geometry happens near constantly. Sprinting around feels obtuse, and you can barely see five feet in front of you, meaning you lose track of civilians and enemies constantly.

2. The gunplay is rough. The weapons are clunky and need to be reloaded constantly. Aiming around corners and through doors is a gamble. Crouching to improve your aim and reduce damage seemingly does nothing.

3. Pickups are too sparse. Since this is a game about murdering civilians, the huge majority of things you're using your ammo to kill aren't replenishing it. Environmental pickups are practically non existent unless you go to a police station, which requires a ♥♥♥♥ to of ammo to infiltrate in the first place.

4. The execute to heal system sucks. The only way to replenish health in this game is to execute enemies, but they have to be injured to do so. However, there's seemingly no consistent way to injure them, so you can't actually get a health "drop" when you need it. In addition, to execute the enemy, you have to literally be standing on top of them, so you can't do it during a fire fight, which is literally the only time you'd ever need to.

5. The writing is embarrassing. If this game was totally and thoroughly ironic, it would be kind of funny. It does not present itself that way however. The main character looks and sounds like a total loser, unappealing and uninteresting from the first cutscene. The lines are stupid and unlikely to impress even the edgiest of middle schoolers. The Dude from postal had a real reason for what he did. Having a psychotic mental break, paranoia and seeing enemies in everyone around you. The burden of society and dehumanization faced in the world drove him to snap. There was depth and meaning behind the events of postal. The Dude was a character and a statement. The guy from Hatred is just a piece of ♥♥♥♥.

6. Controller support is gorked. No ability to rebind buttons in 2015 is a joke. Hold to sprint with left joystick feels awful, insane discrepancy between normal aiming sensitivity and "aim mode" sensitivity.

About the only nice thing to say about this game is that it looks okay. The cutscenes tying into the splash screens and leading into gameplay is fun.

Before I played this game, I had a small wee wee, no friends, no girlfriend, depression and absolutely no will to live. None of these things have changed, but the game is pretty good.

Hatred Review

Before buying the game: I thought and heard this game was a taboo "Postal rip-off" and yeah, it is very comparable to Postal 1 (which I haven't played), however it lacks what the later games would have: the humor. However, what attracted me to Hatred was the taboo aspect. I wanted to explore if it was as bad or as edgy as they say and... not quite, but I can see where people are coming from.

Gunplay Positives: I played most of the game on Normal difficulty, and the game itself plays fine. Weapons feel great to use and the gore and murder in the game is wonderful. I love the long killing animations and the dialogue from NPCs. It does make you feel like some grim reaper wannabe psycho.

Gunplay Negatives: Some of the guns like the shotgun or the SMG feel very clunky to use when killing. Especially aiming with the shotgun—unless you're right in front of the enemy, you will not hit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with it. Another problem I have with the gameplay is the throwables' long wind-up animations that leave you out in the open. Also, throwing things has the problem of you not seeing where it'll precisely land.

Level Positives: Most of the levels are wonderfully created, where you can feel the desperation of law enforcement ramp up slowly as you keep killing and doing side missions. It goes from having only one to two cops pull up to fight you, to them sending two cop cars, to sending entire squads of police. Then later on, they send SWAT teams, and even the army. Levels themselves, for the most part, have a wonderful balance of urban day-to-day life, with loads of people doing their own things before you crash in and destroy it. Most of the environments are highly detailed, and explosive barrels are sprinkled just right to make everything chaotic.

Level Negatives: In the latter half of the levels, the ramp-up in difficulty skyrockets as the military becomes more involved. The last two levels are a perfect example of bad level design, having nothing but mass enemy bullet-sponge spam where they see you before you see them, with less and less regular civilians to execute for HP. The military base especially is absolute ass on any difficulty, with how many enemies you have to gun through just to get the objective and then run back. I will be completely honest: this and the last level gave me most of my criticism over the gunplay and level design. And I will admit, I put the game on the easiest difficulty just to finish the game. I have a skill issue.

Story Positives: It never forgets what it is; you never have any moment of doubt or anything. You are just a hate-filled psycho on a power fantasy.

Story Negatives: The story doesn't go anywhere. This isn't a game where I'm looking for a deep story, but to have none at all is bad. A guy with no name doesn't need a name or emotions, but just a sprinkle of genuine interaction with everything else would be funny. Instead of just hopping from one place to another, there should be more care put into the world around him, even if it's just to destroy it later.

Overall: The game is a "turn off your brain" type with enough edge to cut through a diamond. It's not made for everyone, but I think it doesn't deserve as much criticism as I've personally seen it put through. And in all honesty, go play Postal instead of this.

6/10, would not play again.
